criterion_notes.c1: Examines 31 community-managed decentralized rural drinking-water supply systems (Simple Water Supply System, SiPAS) operating in rural and remote areas of the Brantas River Basin unserved by municipal water utilities, incorporating service continuity, water supply reliability, and affordability among its 26 evaluation indicators (though only at the facility performance-index level rather than household access).
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the literal/plain broad wording of Criterion 2 ('legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory or governance factor'), this paper would pass Criterion 2 itself because its SEM-PLS model includes a latent 'Management aspects' construct covering 'institutional capacity, financial management, human resources', 'governance quality, financial planning', and 'regulatory compliance' (path coefficient = 0.267, p = 0.000). However, even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the overall decision remains exclude (plain_criterion2_decision = 'exclude') because the paper fails Criteria 4 and 5: 'IKManagement' is merely one of three additive sub-indices summed to construct the composite performance score 'IKSiPAS', and no disaggregated service-access outcome is reported. Under the active 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading, Criterion 2 is clearly 'no': the study assesses generic organizational/operator management capacity and an Android field-maintenance application, not any rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, discretion or accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure governing access).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical data from 31 SiPAS sites collected through direct observation, site inventories, and standardized questionnaires completed by SiPAS operators and managers, analyzed via SEM-PLS, GRG nonlinear optimization, t-test validation across 25 observations, and before-and-after operational log comparisons.
criterion_notes.c4: Does not report any disaggregated outcome on household or community access, connection, service availability, continuity, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion. Instead, service continuity, reliability, and affordability are unseparated inputs collapsed alongside technical and managerial items into an overall composite facility performance index (IKSiPAS), and the Android application evaluation reports only operational maintenance metrics (inspection-to-repair cycle time, work-order closure rate, non-revenue-water loss proxy, and change in the technical index ΔIKTechnical).
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis (31 SiPAS facilities surveyed via operators/managers) and analytical methods (SEM-PLS and GRG index construction) are identifiable, but an independent exposure-to-access-outcome relationship cannot be identified: the full 26 questionnaire items are not itemized, the managerial construct (IKManagement) is mathematically a weighted component of the composite outcome index (IKSiPAS = 0.7833 IKTechnical + 0.1011 IKSocial + 0.1156 IKManagement), and the pre/post mobile-app summary omits numerical estimates for any access outcome.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is published in English.

evidence_quotes.quote: Thirty-one SiPAS sites were selected based on criteria such as non-coverage by municipal water utilities (MWUS), reliance on local natural water sources (e.g., springs, rivers, and wells), and community-managed systems.

The questionnaire encompassed 26 performance indicators systematically classified into technical (e.g., infrastructure quality, service continuity, water quality), social (e.g., community participation, affordability, user satisfaction), and management (e.g., institutional capacity, financial management, human resources) aspects, providing a balanced and comprehensive framework for evaluating system performance.

Managerial factors, including governance quality, financial planning, and institutional capacity, explained 26.7% of the variance in system performance. Systems with well-established governance structures, sound financial management, and strong local management institutions demonstrated significantly better performance than those with weaker managerial capabilities.
Data were collected using a mixed-methods approach, combining direct observation, inventory techniques, and standardized questionnaires completed by SiPAS operators and managers.

Four site-level metrics were derived from the monthly inspection-to-repair cycle time (days), work-order closure rate (%), non-revenue-water proxy ("loss," %), and change in the technical index (ΔIKTechnical), and then summarized across locations to characterize central tendency and dispersion [17].

raw_response.exposure: Latent technical, social, and managerial system indicators (e.g., infrastructure quality, community participation, institutional capacity, governance quality, financial management, regulatory compliance) and an Android real-time performance monitoring and work-order application
raw_response.outcome: Composite site-level SiPAS Performance Index (IKSiPAS, weighted sum of technical, social, and management sub-indices) and operational maintenance metrics (monthly inspection-to-repair cycle time, work-order closure rate, non-revenue-water loss proxy, and change in technical sub-index ΔIKTechnical)
raw_response.population_and_sample: 31 community-managed Simple Water Supply System (SiPAS) sites in rural and remote areas of the Brantas River Basin, East Java, surveyed via SiPAS operators and managers (with 25 validation observations and 6 external sites noted for out-of-sample checks)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded at full text (E03: Wrong exposure; also fails Criterion 4 on outcome). This water-resources engineering study constructs and calibrates a composite site-level Performance Index Model (IKSiPAS = 0.7833 IKTechnical + 0.1011 IKSocial + 0.1156 IKManagement) across 31 community-managed rural water supply systems (SiPAS) in Indonesia using SEM-PLS and GRG optimization, and deploys an Android mobile app for real-time maintenance work orders. Under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, it does not examine any rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing service access—its managerial construct captures generic organizational/operator capacity (institutional capacity, financial planning, human resources, generic governance quality/regulatory compliance), and its intervention is a digital maintenance tool. Moreover, even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the study would still be excluded because IKManagement is an additive sub-component of the composite performance score IKSiPAS itself rather than an exposure tested against a disaggregated water access, connection, continuity, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion outcome, and the app evaluation measures only repair cycle time, work-order closure rate, non-revenue-water loss, and ΔIKTechnical.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional operator/manager survey and site inventory modeled with Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) and Generalized Reduced Gradient (GRG) optimization, plus before-and-after operational evaluation of an Android monitoring application
